analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.intro: Plays the battle out many times from the start of every turn on Pokémon Showdown's simulator, in your browser, to estimate {name}'s chance to win at each point. About {s} seconds for a typical battle.
analysis.boardLabel: In battle at the start of turn {turn}
analysis.noKeyMoments: No turn moved the win chance by more than the simulations' own margin of error.
analysis.noMissed: No missed KOs (a move {name} had shown with a 50%+ chance to KO, not used) and no switch-ins into a likely KO.
analysis.howBody: From {name}'s side, using only what the battle showed: each Pokémon's HP, status, stat stages, hazards, weather and Tera as they stood at the start of the turn. Every turn was played out to the end {n} times on average by the computer's Hard strategy for both sides; the shaded band is the 95% confidence interval (up to ±{widest}).
analysis.howDoubles: Double battles play both Pokémon of each side together: targets picked on the damage calc, spread moves at their 75% (and the partner they hit), Protect, Fake Out and shared KOs.
analysis.assumedMoves: {n, plural, one {{n} move was} other {{n} moves were}} assumed rather than seen. Pokémon that came out later in the battle are counted from the start. Missed KOs use only moves {name}'s Pokémon actually used; KO chances are the damage calc's non-critical rolls times accuracy.

stats.title: Battle stats
stats.noTurning: No single turn moved the win chance by more than the simulations' margin of error: this one was decided bit by bit.
stats.meterLabel: Luck {score}, where luck alone usually lands within ±{sd}
stats.howLuck1: Every crit, miss and side effect (burn, paralysis, freeze, poison, sleep, confusion, flinch, stat changes) is counted against the odds it had when it happened, from the move's accuracy, crit rate and effect chance with the stat stages, weather and the items and abilities the battle had shown. Each one that came off above its odds is +1 for the side it helped; one expected but not seen is the same in reverse. A damage roll counts up to ±0.5 (a top roll +0.5, an average one 0).
stats.howLuck2: The expected numbers are estimates: an item or ability nobody saw (Scope Lens, Serene Grace, BrightPowder…) comes from the most likely set, and damage rolls are placed with the damage calc on assumed sets, only where the HP bar can tell ({placed} of {total} plain hits). The usual range is how far luck alone strays in a battle with this many chances (one standard deviation).
stats.rollsDetail: (yours: {ownHigh} high, {ownLow} low of {own}; theirs: {theirHigh} high, {theirLow} low of {their})
stats.workNote: Damage as % of a Pokémon's max HP (100% = one whole Pokémon)
